claims.dateText: 三十五年...六月中，病熱，六日薨

translationRepairs: That November the emperor deposed the heir from the Su clan; the empress dowager began to hope openly that the king of Liang might succeed him.
That November the emperor deposed Crown Prince Li; the empress dowager privately hoped that the king of Liang might succeed him.
栗太子 is Crown Prince Li, while 心欲 expresses inward intent; 'privately hoped' corrects both the invented Su clan and the proposal's contradictory 'openly.'
In the eleventh month, the sovereign deposed the Crown Prince of Su; the empress dowager in her heart wished to make the King of Liang heir.
In the eleventh month, the sovereign deposed Crown Prince Li; the empress dowager in her heart wished to make the King of Liang heir.
栗太子 is Crown Prince Li; “Crown Prince of Su” misreads 栗.

In Yuanshi 2 Wang Mang, as marquis of Xindu, petitioned the Grand Empress Dowager to revive a fallen line and enfeoffed Nian’s nephew Ruyi as king of Guangzong to continue the sacrifices to King Xiao of Dai’s queen.
In Yuanshi 2, Wang Mang, Marquis of Xindu, petitioned the Grand Empress Dowager to restore the extinct line. Nian's nephew Ruyi was enfeoffed as King of Guangzong to continue King Xiao of Dai's line.
奉代孝王后 means to continue King Xiao of Dai's line, not to serve his queen; splitting the sentence also makes clear that Wang Mang petitioned and Ruyi was enfeoffed.

Li in fear took off his cap and replied: “Li in youth lost father and mother; orphaned and weak he dwelt in the deep palace; alone with eunuchs, maids, and concubines he lived; gradually he was steeped in the customs of a small state; added to this his substance and nature are low and stupid; there is an posture that cannot be shifted.

“An posture” is ungrammatical English; “a posture” is the correct article before the consonant onset of posture.
